subsection.heading: Short Title.—
subsection.content: This Act may be cited as the “Water Resources Development Act of 1999”.

section.heading: USE OF CONTINUING CONTRACTS FOR CONSTRUCTION OF CERTAIN PROJECTS.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: Notwithstanding any other provision of law, the Secretary shall not implement a fully allocated funding policy with respect to a water resource project if initiation of construction has occurred but sufficient funds are not available to complete the project.

subsection.heading: Continuing Contracts.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall enter into a continuing contract for a project described in subsection (a).

subsection.heading: Initiation of Construction Clarified.—
subsection.chapeau: For the purposes of this section, initiation of construction for a project occurs on the date of enactment of an Act that appropriates funds for the project from 1 of the following appropriation accounts:

paragraph.content: Construction, General.
Operation and Maintenance, General.
Flood Control, Mississippi River and Tributaries.

section.heading: SHORELINE AND RIVERINE PROTECTION AND RESTORATION.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.chapeau: The Secretary may carry out studies and projects to—

paragraph.content: reduce flood and hurricane and storm damage hazards; or
restore the natural functions and values of rivers and shorelines throughout the United States.

subparagraph.heading: Studies.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary may carry out studies to identify appropriate measures for—

clause.content: the reduction of flood and hurricane and storm damage hazards, including measures for erosion mitigation and bank stabilization; or
the conservation and restoration of the natural functions and values of rivers and shorelines.

subparagraph.heading: Projects.—
subparagraph.content: Subject to subsection (f)(2), in carrying out subsection (a), the Secretary may design and implement projects described in subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Consultation and coordination.—
paragraph.content: The studies and projects carried out under this section shall be conducted, to the maximum extent practicable, in consultation and coordination with the Federal Emergency Management Agency and other appropriate Federal agencies, and in consultation and coordination with appropriate State and local agencies and tribes.

paragraph.heading: Nonstructural approaches.—
paragraph.content: The studies and projects shall emphasize, to the maximum extent practicable and appropriate, nonstructural approaches to preventing or reducing flood and hurricane and storm damages, including the use of natural features or nature-based features.

paragraph.heading: Participation.—
paragraph.content: The studies and projects shall be conducted, to the maximum extent practicable, in cooperation with State and local agencies and tribes to ensure the coordination of local flood and hurricane and storm damage reduction or riverine, shoreline, and wetland restoration studies with projects that conserve, restore, and manage hydrologic and hydraulic regimes and restore the natural functions and values of floodplains and coastal barriers.

paragraph.heading: Studies.—
paragraph.content: Studies conducted under this section shall be subject to cost sharing in accordance with section 105 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2215), except that the first $200,000 of the costs of a study conducted under this section shall be at Federal expense.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Design and construction of a project under this section that includes a nonstructural measure, a natural feature or nature-based feature, or an environmental restoration measure, shall be subject to cost sharing in accordance with section 103 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2213), except that the non-Federal share of the cost to design and construct such a project benefitting an economically disadvantaged community (including economically disadvantaged communities located in urban and rural areas) shall be 10 percent.

subparagraph.heading: Items provided by non-federal interests.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interests shall provide all land, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas, and relocations necessary for such projects.

subparagraph.heading: Credit.—
subparagraph.content: The value of such land, easements, rights-of-way, dredged material disposal areas, and relocations shall be credited toward the payment required under this paragraph.

paragraph.heading: Structural flood control or hurricane and storm damage reduction projects.—
paragraph.content: Any structural flood control or hurricane and storm damage reduction projects carried out under this section shall be subject to cost sharing in accordance with section 103 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (33 U.S.C. 2213), except that the non-Federal share of the cost to design and construct such a project benefitting an economically disadvantaged community (including economically disadvantaged communities located in urban and rural areas) shall be 10 percent.

paragraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
paragraph.content: The non-Federal interests shall be responsible for all costs associated with operating, maintaining, replacing, repairing, and rehabilitating all projects carried out under this section.

subsection.heading: Project Justification.—
subsection.chapeau: Notwithstanding any requirement for economic justification established under section 209 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962–2), the Secretary may implement a project under this section if the Secretary determines that the project—

paragraph.content: will significantly reduce potential flood, hurricane and storm, or erosion damages;
will improve the quality of the environment; and
is justified considering all costs and beneficial outputs of the project.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall examine appropriate locations, including—

subparagraph.content: Pima County, Arizona, at Paseo De Las Iglesias and Rillito River;
Coachella Valley, Riverside County, California;
Los Angeles and San Gabriel Rivers, California;
Murrieta Creek, California;
Napa River Valley watershed, California, at Yountville, St. Helena, Calistoga, and American Canyon;
Santa Clara basin, California, at Upper Guadalupe River and Tributaries, San Francisquito Creek, and Upper Penitencia Creek;
Pond Creek, Kentucky;
Red River of the North, Minnesota, North Dakota, and South Dakota;
Connecticut River, New Hampshire;
Pine Mount Creek, New Jersey;
Southwest Valley, Albuquerque, New Mexico;
Upper Delaware River, New York;
Briar Creek, North Carolina;
Chagrin River, Ohio;
Mill Creek, Cincinnati, Ohio;
Tillamook County, Oregon;
Willamette River basin, Oregon;
Blair County, Pennsylvania, at Altoona and Frankstown Township;
Delaware River, Pennsylvania;
Schuylkill River, Pennsylvania;
Providence County, Rhode Island;
Shenandoah River, Virginia;
Lincoln Creek, Wisconsin;
Perry Creek, Iowa;
Lester, St. Louis, East Savanna, and Floodwood Rivers, Duluth, Minnesota;
Lower Hudson River and tributaries, New York;
Susquehanna River watershed, Bradford County, Pennsylvania;
Clear Creek, Harris, Galveston, and Brazoria Counties, Texas;
Ascension Parish, Louisiana;
East Baton Rouge Parish, Louisiana;
Iberville Parish, Louisiana;
Livingston Parish, Louisiana; and
Pointe Coupee Parish, Louisiana.

paragraph.heading: Priority projects.—
paragraph.chapeau: In carrying out this section, the Secretary shall prioritize projects for the following locations:

subparagraph.content: Delaware beaches and watersheds, Delaware.
Louisiana Coastal Area, Louisiana.
Great Lakes Shores and Watersheds.
Oregon Coastal Area and Willamette River basin, Oregon.
Upper Missouri River Basin.
Ohio River Tributaries and their watersheds, West Virginia.
Chesapeake Bay watershed and Maryland beaches, Maryland.
City of Southport, North Carolina.
Maumee River, Ohio.
Los Angeles and San Gabriel Rivers, California.
Kentucky River and its tributaries and watersheds.
Shoreline of the State of Connecticut.
Winooski River tributary watershed, Vermont.

paragraph.heading: All projects.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall not implement any project under this section until—

subparagraph.content: the Secretary submits to the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate and the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives a written notification describing the project and the determinations made under subsection (d)(1); and
21 calendar days have elapsed after the date on which the notification was received by the committees.

paragraph.heading: Projects requiring specific authorization.—
paragraph.content: If the Federal share of the cost to design and construct a project under this section exceeds $15,000,000, the Secretary may only carry out the project if Congress enacts a law authorizing the Secretary to carry out the project.

paragraph.heading: Economically disadvantaged community.—
paragraph.content: The term “economically disadvantaged community” has the meaning given the term as defined by the Secretary under section 160 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2020 (33 U.S.C. 2201 note).

paragraph.heading: Natural feature; nature-based feature.—
paragraph.content: The terms “natural feature” and “nature-based feature” have the meanings given those terms in section 1184(a) of the Water Resources Development Act of 2016 (33 U.S.C. 2289a(a)).

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: During fiscal years 1999 through 2002, the Secretary may withhold from the special account established under section 4(i)(1)(A) of the Land and Water Conservation Fund Act of 1965 (16 U.S.C. 460l–a(i)(1)(A)) 100 percent of the amount of receipts above a baseline of $34,000,000 per each fiscal year received from fees imposed at recreation sites under the administrative jurisdiction of the Department of the Army under section 4(b) of that Act (16 U.S.C. 460l–a(b)).

paragraph.heading: Use.—
paragraph.content: The amounts withheld shall be retained by the Secretary and shall be available, without further Act of appropriation, for expenditure by the Secretary in accordance with subsection (b).

paragraph.heading: Availability.—
paragraph.content: The amounts withheld shall remain available until September 30, 2005.

subsection.heading: Use of Amounts Withheld.—
subsection.chapeau: In order to increase the quality of the visitor experience at public recreational areas and to enhance the protection of resources, the amounts withheld under subsection (a) may be used only for—

paragraph.content: repair and maintenance projects (including projects relating to health and safety);
interpretation;
signage;
habitat or facility enhancement;
resource preservation;
annual operation (including fee collection);
maintenance; and
law enforcement related to public use.

subsection.heading: Availability.—
subsection.content: Each amount withheld by the Secretary shall be available for expenditure, without further Act of appropriation, at the specific project from which the amount, above baseline, is collected.

section.heading: WEST BANK OF THE MISSISSIPPI RIVER (EAST OF HARVEY CANAL), LOUISIANA.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The project to prevent flood damage and for hurricane damage reduction, west bank of the Mississippi River (east of Harvey Canal), Louisiana, authorized by section 401(b) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (100 Stat. 4128) and section 101(a)(17) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1996 (110 Stat. 3665), is modified to direct the Secretary to continue Federal operation, maintenance, rehabilitation, repair, and replacement of the portion of the project included in the report of the Chief of Engineers dated May 1, 1995, referred to as “Algiers Canal Levees”.

subsection.heading: Combination of Projects.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall carry out work authorized as part of the Westwego to Harvey Canal project, the East of Harvey Canal project, and the Lake Cataouatche modifications as a single project, to be known as the “West Bank and Vicinity, New Orleans, Louisiana, Hurricane Protection Project”, with a combined total cost of $280,300,000.

subsection.heading: Cost Sharing.—
subsection.content: The non-Federal share of the cost of the project described in subsection (b) shall be 35 percent.

section.heading: MISSOURI RIVER MITIGATION PROJECT, MISSOURI, KANSAS, IOWA, AND NEBRASKA.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The project for mitigation of fish and wildlife losses, Missouri River Bank Stabilization and Navigation Project, Missouri, Kansas, Iowa, and Nebraska, authorized by section 601(a) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (100 Stat. 4143) is modified to increase by 118,650 acres the amount of land and interests in land to be acquired for the project.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary, in conjunction with the States of Missouri, Kansas, Iowa, and Nebraska, shall conduct a study to determine the cost of restoring, under the authority of the Missouri River fish and wildlife mitigation project, a total of 118,650 acres of lost Missouri River fish and wildlife habitat.

paragraph.heading: Report.—
paragraph.content: Not later than 180 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall report to Congress on the results of the study.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.chapeau: The Secretary shall consult with other Federal agencies to determine if lands or interests in lands acquired by such other Federal agencies—

subparagraph.content: meet the purposes of the Missouri River Mitigation Project, Missouri, Kansas, Iowa, and Nebraska, authorized by section 601(a) of the Water Resources Development Act of 1986 (100 Stat. 4143; 113 Stat. 306; 121 Stat. 1155); and
whether such lands are restricted by such other Federal agencies from being applied toward the total number of acres required under subsection (a).

paragraph.heading: Application of lands.—
paragraph.content: Upon making a determination under paragraph (1) that lands or interests in lands acquired by a Federal agency meet the purposes of the project described in paragraph (1)(A) and that such lands are not otherwise restricted, the Secretary shall apply the lands or interests in lands acquired toward the total number of acres required under subsection (a), regardless of the source of the Federal funds used to acquire such lands or interests in lands.

paragraph.heading: Savings provision.—
paragraph.content: Nothing in this subsection authorizes any transfer of administrative jurisdiction over any lands or interests in lands acquired by a Federal agency that are applied toward the total number of acres required under subsection (a) pursuant to this subsection.

section.heading: WESTERN LAKE ERIE BASIN, OHIO, INDIANA, AND MICHIGAN.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall conduct a study to develop measures to improve flood risk management, hurricane and storm damage risk reduction, navigation, water quality, recreation, and fish and wildlife habitat in a comprehensive manner in the western Lake Erie basin, Ohio, Indiana, and Michigan, including watersheds of the Maumee, Ottawa, and Portage Rivers.

subsection.heading: Cooperation.—
subsection.chapeau: In carrying out any study under this section, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: cooperate with interested Federal, State, and local agencies and nongovernmental organizations; and
consider all relevant programs of the agencies.

subsection.heading: Treatment of Studies.—
subsection.content: Any study carried out by the Secretary under this section after the date of enactment of the Water Resources Development Act of 2024 shall be treated as a continuation of the initial study carried out under this section.

subsection.heading: Projects.—
subsection.content: A project resulting from a study carried out under this section may be implemented pursuant to section 212.

section.heading: JOHN GLENN GREAT LAKES BASIN PROGRAM.

paragraph.heading: Study.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall conduct a comprehensive study of the Great Lakes region to ensure the future use, management, and protection of water resources and related resources of the Great Lakes basin.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: As expeditiously as possible, but not later than 3 years after the date of enactment of this Act, and every 2 years thereafter, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Transportation and Infrastructure of the House of Representatives and the Committee on Environment and Public Works of the Senate a report outlining a strategic plan for Corps of Engineers programs and proposed Corps of Engineers projects in the Great Lakes basin.

clause.chapeau: details of projects in the Great Lakes region relating to—

subclause.content: navigation improvements, maintenance, and operations for commercial and recreational vessels;
technical and planning assistance to States and remedial action planning committees;
sediment transport analysis, sediment management planning, and activities to support prevention of excess sediment loadings;
flood damage reduction and shoreline erosion prevention; and
all other relevant activities of the Corps of Engineers; and

clause.content: an analysis of factors limiting use of programs and authorities of the Corps of Engineers in existence on the date of enactment of this Act in the Great Lakes basin, including the need for new or modified authorities.

paragraph.heading: Authorization of appropriations.—
paragraph.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $1,000,000 for the period of fiscal years 2000 through 2003.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Not later than 90 days after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary shall request each Federal agency that may possess information relevant to the Great Lakes biohydrological system to provide an inventory of all such information in the possession of the agency.

subparagraph.heading: Relevant information.—
subparagraph.chapeau: For the purpose of subparagraph (A), relevant information includes information on—

clause.content: biological aspects of the system influenced by and influencing water quantity and water movement;
meteorological projections and the impacts of weather conditions on Great Lakes water levels; and
other Great Lakes biohydrological system data relevant to sustainable water use management.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.chapeau: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, in consultation with the States, Indian tribes, and Federal agencies, and after requesting information from the provinces and the federal government of Canada, shall—

clause.content: analyze the information for consistency and gaps; and

submit to Congress, the International Joint Commission, and the Great Lakes States a report that includes recommendations on ways to improve the information base on the biohydrological dynamics of the Great Lakes ecosystem as a whole, so as to support environmentally sound decisions regarding diversions and consumptive uses of Great Lakes water.

subparagraph.heading: Recommendations.—
subparagraph.content: The recommendations in the report under subparagraph (A) shall include recommendations relating to the resources and funds necessary for implementing improvement of the information base.

subparagraph.heading: Considerations.—
subparagraph.chapeau: In developing the report under subparagraph (A), the Secretary, in cooperation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Transportation, and the heads of other agencies as appropriate, shall consider and report on the status of the issues described and recommendations made in—

clause.content: the Report of the International Joint Commission to the Governments of the United States and Canada under the 1977 reference issued in 1985; and

the 1993 Report of the International Joint Commission to the Governments of Canada and the United States on Methods of Alleviating Adverse Consequences of Fluctuating Water Levels in the Great Lakes St. Lawrence Basin.

subsection.heading: Great Lakes Recreational Boating.—
subsection.content: Not later than 18 months after the date of enactment of this Act, the Secretary, using information and studies in existence on the date of enactment of this Act to the extent practicable, and in cooperation with the Great Lakes States, shall submit to Congress a report detailing the economic benefits of recreational boating in the Great Lakes basin, particularly at harbors benefiting from operation and maintenance projects of the Corps of Engineers.

subsection.heading: Cooperation.—
subsection.chapeau: In undertaking activities under this section, the Secretary shall—

paragraph.content: encourage public participation; and
cooperate, and, as appropriate, collaborate, with Great Lakes States, tribal governments, and Canadian federal, provincial, and tribal governments.

subsection.heading: Water Use Activities and Policies.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide technical assistance to the Great Lakes States to develop interstate guidelines to improve the consistency and efficiency of State-level water use activities and policies in the Great Lakes basin.

subsection.heading: Cost Sharing.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may seek and accept funds from non-Federal entities to be used to pay up to 25 percent of the cost of carrying out subsections (b), (c), (d), and (e).

subsection.heading: In-Kind Contributions for Study.—
subsection.content: The non-Federal interest may provide up to 100 percent of the non-Federal share required under subsection (f) in the form of in-kind services and materials.

section.heading: ABANDONED AND INACTIVE NONCOAL MINE RESTORATION.

subsection.heading: In General.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide technical, planning, and design assistance to Federal and non-Federal interests for carrying out projects to address water quality problems caused by drainage and related activities from abandoned and inactive noncoal mines.

subsection.heading: Specific Measures.—
subsection.chapeau: Assistance provided under subsection (a) may be in support of projects for the purposes of—

paragraph.content: managing drainage from abandoned and inactive noncoal mines;
restoring and protecting streams, rivers, wetlands, other waterbodies, and riparian areas degraded by drainage from abandoned and inactive noncoal mines; and

demonstrating management practices and innovative and alternative treatment technologies to minimize or eliminate adverse environmental effects associated with drainage from abandoned and inactive noncoal mines.

subsection.heading: Non-Federal Share.—
subsection.content: The non-Federal share of the cost of assistance under subsection (a) shall be 50 percent, except that the Federal share with respect to projects located on land owned by the United States, on land held in trust by the Secretary of the Interior on behalf of, and for the benefit of, an Indian Tribe, or on restricted land of any Indian Tribe, shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Effect on Authority of Secretary of the Interior.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section affects the authority of the Secretary of the Interior under title IV of the Surface Mining Control and Reclamation Act of 1977 (30 U.S.C. 1231 et seq.).

subsection.heading: Technology Database for Reclamation of Abandoned Mines.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide assistance to non-Federal and nonprofit entities to develop, manage, and maintain a database of conventional and innovative, cost-effective technologies for reclamation of abandoned and inactive noncoal mine sites. Such assistance shall be provided through the Restoration of Abandoned Mine Sites Program managed by the Albuquerque District Office of the Corps of Engineers.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $50,000,000.

subsection.heading: Definition of Northeastern Minnesota.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “northeastern Minnesota” means the counties of Cook, Lake, St. Louis, Koochiching, Itasca, Cass, Crow Wing, Aitkin, Carlton, Pine, Kanabec, Mille Lacs, Morrison, Beltrami, Hubbard, Wadena, Isanti, and Chisago, Minnesota.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a pilot program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in northeastern Minnesota.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for waterrelated environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in northeastern Minnesota, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, water supply and related facilities, environmental restoration, and surface water resource protection and development.

subsection.heading: Public Ownership Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide assistance for a project under this section only if the project is publicly owned.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Before providing assistance under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a local cooperation agreement with a non-Federal interest to provide for design and construction of the project to be carried out with the assistance.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each local cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall provide for the following:

subparagraph.heading: Plan.—
subparagraph.content: Development by the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal and State officials, of a facilities or resource protection and development plan, including appropriate engineering plans and specifications.

subparagraph.heading: Legal and institutional structures.—
subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Federal share of project costs under each local cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall be 75 percent. The Federal share may be in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for design work.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for the reasonable costs of design work completed by the non-Federal interest before entering into a local cooperation agreement with the Secretary for a project.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for interest.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the funding of the non-Federal share of the costs of a project that is the subject of an agreement under this section, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest incurred in providing - the non-Federal share of the project’s costs.

subparagraph.heading: Land, easements, and rights-of-way credit.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including all reasonable costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but not to exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed with assistance provided under this section shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section waives, limits, or otherwise affects the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Nonprofit Entities.—
subsection.content: In accordance with section 221(b) of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d–5b(b)), for any project carried out under this section, a non-Federal interest may include a nonprofit entity with the consent of the affected local government.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $80,000,000 for the period beginning with fiscal year 2000, to remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: Corps of Engineers Expenses.—
subsection.content: Not more than 10 percent of the amounts appropriated to carry out this section may be used by the Corps of Engineers district offices to administer projects under this section at Federal expense.

subsection.heading: Definition of Native Corporation.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “Native Corporation” has the meaning given the term in section 3 of the Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act (43 U.S.C. 1602).

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $45,000,000 for the period beginning with fiscal year 2000, to remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: Definition of Northern West Virginia.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “northern West Virginia” means the counties of Barbour, Berkeley, Brooke, Doddridge, Grant, Hampshire, Hancock, Hardy, Harrison, Jefferson, Lewis, Marion, Marshall, Mineral, Morgan, Monongalia, Ohio, Pleasants, Preston, Randolph, Ritchie, Taylor, Tucker, Tyler, Upshur, Wetzel, and Wood, West Virginia.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a pilot program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in northern West Virginia.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for water-related environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in northern West Virginia, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, water supply and related facilities, and surface water resource protection and development.

subsection.heading: Public Ownership Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide assistance for a project under this section only if the project is publicly owned.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Before providing assistance under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a local cooperation agreement with a non-Federal interest to provide for design and construction of the project to be carried out with the assistance.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each local cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall provide for the following:

subparagraph.heading: Plan.—
subparagraph.content: Development by the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal and State officials, of a facilities or resource protection and development plan, including appropriate engineering plans and specifications.

subparagraph.heading: Legal and institutional structures.—
subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: Except as provided in subparagraph (F), the Federal share of the project costs under each local cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall be 75 percent. The Federal share may be in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for design work.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for the reasonable costs of design work completed by the non-Federal interest before entering into a local cooperation agreement with the Secretary for a project. The credit for the design work shall not exceed 6 percent of the total construction costs of the project.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for interest.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the funding of the non-Federal share of a project that is the subject of an agreement under this section, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest incurred in providing the non-Federal share of the project’s costs.

subparagraph.heading: Land, easements, and rights-of-way credit.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including all reasonable costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but not to exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed with assistance provided under this section shall be 100 percent.

subparagraph.heading: Exception.—
subparagraph.content: In the case of a project benefitting an economically disadvantaged community (as defined by the Secretary under section 160 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2020 (33 U.S.C. 2201 note)), the Federal share of the project costs under the applicable local cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall be 90 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section waives, limits, or otherwise affects the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $150,000,000 for the period beginning with fiscal year 2000, to remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: Nonprofit Entities.—
subsection.content: In accordance with section 221(b) of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-5b(b)), for any project undertaken under this section, a non-Federal interest may include a nonprofit entity with the consent of the affected local government.

subsection.heading: Corps of Engineers Expenses.—
subsection.content: Not more than 10 percent of the amounts appropriated to carry out this section may be used by the Corps of Engineers district offices to administer projects under this section at Federal expense.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a pilot program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in Mississippi.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for waterrelated environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in Mississippi, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, elimination or control of combined sewer overflows, water supply and related facilities, environmental restoration, surface water resource protection and development, stormwater management, drainage systems, and water quality enhancement.

subsection.heading: Public Ownership Requirement.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may provide assistance for a project under this section only if the project is publicly owned.

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Before providing assistance under this section, the Secretary shall enter into a local cooperation agreement with a non-Federal interest to provide for design and construction of the project to be carried out with the assistance.

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each local cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall provide for the following: (A) PLAN.-Development by the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal and State officials, of a facilities or resource protection and development plan, including appropriate engineering plans and specifications.

subparagraph.heading: Legal and institutional structures.—
subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

subparagraph.heading: In general.—
subparagraph.content: The Federal share of project costs under each local cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall be 75 percent. The Federal share may be in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for design work.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for the reasonable costs of design work completed by the non-Federal interest before entering into a local cooperation agreement with the Secretary for a project. The credit for the design work shall not exceed 6 percent of the total construction costs of the project.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for interest.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the funding of the non-Federal share of the costs of a project that is the subject of an agreement under this section, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest incurred in providing the non-Federal share of the project’s costs.

subparagraph.heading: Land, easements, and rights-of-way credit.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including all reasonable costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the construction, operation, and maintenance of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but not to exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed with assistance provided under this section shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section waives, limits, or otherwise affects the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than December 31, 2001, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the pilot program carried out under this section, including recommendations concerning whether the program should be implemented on a national basis.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $300,000,000, to remain available until expended.

subsection.heading: Definition of Central New Mexico.—
subsection.content: In this section, the term “central New Mexico” means the counties of Bernalillo, Colfax, Sandoval, and Valencia, New Mexico.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a pilot program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in central New Mexico.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.content: Assistance under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for waterrelated environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in central New Mexico, including projects for wastewater treatment and related facilities, water supply, conservation, water reuse, and related facilities, stormwater retention and remediation, environmental restoration, and surface water resource protection and development.

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary shall establish a program to provide environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in Ohio and North Dakota.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.chapeau: Assistance under this section may be in the form of design and construction assistance for waterrelated environmental infrastructure and resource protection and development projects in Ohio and North Dakota, including projects for—

paragraph.content: wastewater treatment and related facilities;
combined sewer overflow, water supply, storage, treatment, and related facilities;
mine drainage;
environmental restoration; and
surface water resource protection and development.

subsection.heading: Public Ownership Requirement.—

paragraph.heading: In general.—

paragraph.heading: Requirements.—
paragraph.chapeau: Each project cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall provide for the following:

subparagraph.heading: Plan.—
subparagraph.content: Development by the Secretary, in consultation with appropriate Federal and State officials, of a facilities development plan or resource protection plan, including appropriate plans and specifications.

subparagraph.heading: Legal and institutional structures.—
subparagraph.content: Establishment of such legal and institutional structures as are necessary to ensure the effective long-term operation of the project by the non-Federal interest.

clause.heading: In general.—
clause.content: Except as provided in clause (iii), the Federal share of project costs under each project cooperation agreement entered into under this subsection shall be 75 percent.

clause.heading: Form.—
clause.content: The Federal share may be in the form of grants or reimbursements of project costs.

clause.heading: Exception.—
clause.content: The non-Federal share of the cost of a project under this section benefitting an economically disadvantaged community (as defined by the Secretary under section 160 of the Water Resources Development Act of 2020 (33 U.S.C. 2201 note)) shall be 10 percent.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for design work.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for the reasonable costs of design work completed by the non-Federal interest before entering into a project cooperation agreement with the Secretary.

subparagraph.heading: Credit for certain financing costs.—
subparagraph.content: In case of a delay in the reimbursement of the non-Federal share of the costs of a project, the non-Federal interest shall receive credit for reasonable interest and other associated financing costs necessary for the non-Federal interest to provide the non-Federal share of the project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal interest shall receive credit for land, easements, rights-of-way, and relocations provided by the non-Federal interest toward the non-Federal share of project costs (including costs associated with obtaining permits necessary for the placement of the project on publicly owned or controlled land), but not to exceed 25 percent of total project costs.

subparagraph.heading: Operation and maintenance.—
subparagraph.content: The non-Federal share of operation and maintenance costs for projects constructed under an agreement entered into under this subsection shall be 100 percent.

subsection.heading: Applicability of Other Federal and State Laws.—
subsection.content: Nothing in this section waives, limits, or otherwise affects the applicability of any provision of Federal or State law that would otherwise apply to a project to be carried out with assistance provided under this section.

subsection.heading: Nonprofit Entities.—
subsection.content: In accordance with section 221 of the Flood Control Act of 1970 (42 U.S.C. 1962d-5b), a non-Federal interest for any project carried out under this section may include a nonprofit entity, with the consent of the affected local government.

subsection.heading: Report.—
subsection.content: Not later than December 31, 2001, the Secretary shall submit to Congress a report on the results of the program carried out under this section, including recommendations concerning whether the program should be implemented on a national basis.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Appropriations.—
subsection.content: There is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $300,000,000 for Ohio and $100,000,000 for North Dakota.

subsection.heading: Authorization of Additional Appropriations.—
subsection.content: In addition to amounts authorized under subsection (h), there is authorized to be appropriated to carry out this section $100,000,000, to be divided between the States referred to in subsection (a).

subsection.heading: Establishment of Program.—
subsection.content: The Secretary may establish a program for providing environmental assistance to non-Federal interests in Arizona, rural Idaho, Montana, rural Nevada, NewMexico, rural Utah, and Wyoming.

subsection.heading: Form of Assistance.—
subsection.chapeau: Assistance under this section may be in the form of—

paragraph.chapeau: design and construction assistance for water-related environmental infrastructure, including natural and nature-based infrastructure and resource protection and development in Arizona, Idaho, Montana, rural Nevada, New Mexico, rural Utah, and Wyoming, including projects for—

subparagraph.content: wastewater treatment and related facilities;
water supply and related facilities;
environmental restoration;
surface water resource protection and development; and
drought resilience measures; and

paragraph.heading: In general.—
paragraph.content: Assistance under this section shall be made available to all eligible States and locales described in subsection (b) consistent with program priorities determined by the Secretary in accordance with criteria developed by the Secretary to establish the program priorities.

paragraph.heading: Selection of projects.—
paragraph.chapeau: In selecting projects for assistance under this section, the Secretary shall give priority to a project located in an eligible State or local entity for which the project sponsor is prepared to—

subparagraph.content: execute a new or amended project cooperation agreement; and
commence promptly after the date of enactment of the Water Resources Development Act of 2016.

paragraph.heading: Rural projects.—
paragraph.content: The Secretary shall consider a project authorized under this section and an environmental infrastructure project authorized under section 219 of the Water Resources Development Act of 1992 (Public Law 102–580; 106 Stat. 4835) for new starts on the same basis as any other similarly funded project.
